The topic of organizational change within the Danish clinical quality databases is highlighted by recent structural updates to data collection processes. Specifically, an operational shift was implemented involving the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database) and the broader [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] (the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program) [^src1]. This change centers on the integration of practicing medical specialists into the national data collection framework. As of June 1, 2023, a formal affiliation with practicing cardiologists was established, enabling them to actively collect and submit clinical data to the registry [^src1]. This expansion of data contributors represents a significant organizational change, broadening the scope of the database beyond traditional hospital-based reporting to include specialized outpatient and private practice care.
